Investors asking where to put new money should start with the boring answer. A total market fund such as Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF (VTI) captures the entire US equity risk premium at an expense ratio of 0.03%, and over the last twenty years it has compounded at roughly 9% a year with volatility near 16% and a maximum drawdown of 35%.

Bonds are no longer a zero-yield afterthought. BND yields over 4%, and IEF offers duration that has historically rallied when equities fall, though that correlation is not guaranteed. Risks include a repeat of 2022, when stocks and bonds fell together as inflation reaccelerated.

For real assets, GLD remains the cleanest inflation hedge available in a brokerage account. Its correlation to the S&P 500 is close to zero, which is the whole point of owning it.

Bear case: if real rates rise further, both long bonds and gold suffer while equities may not. Disclosure: the author is long VTI and BND. Source: fund documents and public price data.

Standard deviation, Sharpe ratio and maximum drawdown should drive position sizing, not conviction. Rebalance annually and keep your time horizon in mind.
